title: **Three Iranian Soldiers Return Home After Six Months in Captivity**
text:
**Three Iranian Soldiers Return Home After Six Months in Captivity**"

"On August 28th, After six months of separation and captivity, three young soldiers from the Iranian Army who served on the naval vessel IRIS Lavan have returned to their hometown of Darab in Fars Province. They were welcomed back by their families, friends, local residents, and officials."

"**Background on the IRIS Lavan Incident**"

"The IRIS Lavan is a *Hengam*-class landing ship of Iran's naval forces, named after Lavan Island."

"The vessel was part of Iran's naval contingent participating in India's International Fleet Review and the MILAN 2026 multinational naval exercise in Visakhapatnam in February 2026. On March 4, 2026, the IRIS Lavan docked at the Port of Kochi in southern India after experiencing serious technical malfunctions. This occurred on the same day that the Iranian frigate IRIS Dena was struck and sunk by a US submarine in the Indian Ocean."

"India granted the IRIS Lavan permission to dock on "humanitarian grounds", and its 183 crew members were accommodated at Indian naval facilities in Kochi. Subsequently, India repatriated the non-essential crew members of the vessel. However, it appears that three of the crew members were held in captivity during this period."

"**Note on the return:** The three soldiers returned to Darab on August 28 (approximately 17 hours prior to the time of this report). A welcome ceremony was held for them at the Pir Morad Martyrs' Cemetery in Darab, where they were reunited with their families and received by local officials and community members.
